detailedExplanation: Verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Physics Curriculum Outline 2026–27 and aligned to AQA GCSE Physics 8463.
Power is the rate at which energy is transferred, or the rate at which work is done. Use P = E/t and, where relevant, P = W/t.
One watt means one joule of energy transferred per second. A higher-power device transfers the same amount of energy in less time, or more energy in the same time.
Energy and power are not interchangeable. Energy is measured in joules, whereas power is measured in watts.
In multi-step questions, identify what the question gives: if power and time are known, rearrange to E = Pt; if energy and time are known, divide energy by time.
examTips: Write P = E/t first and check that time is in seconds unless the units have been deliberately matched.
Use the command word and number of marks to judge the number of distinct points required.
For calculations: write the equation, substitute with consistent units, show working and give the final unit.
For practical questions: identify the independent, dependent and control variables and explain how data quality is improved.
